wordmark.purpose: The LIA mark, set as a typed card-stock plate at the left of the drawer label. Typography, not an image.

notation.purpose: Every measured quantity: dimensions, counts, densities, device ids, build stamps. Tabular figures.

tray-title.purpose: Ruled-off uppercase heading of an open tray.

commit-label.purpose: The word on the single primary key: Connect, Pairing, Print.

body.purpose: Default UI speech in the sans face.

label.purpose: Drawer tab labels and small control text.

caption.purpose: Menu field labels and colophon, in the notation face.

shadows.name: lift-card
shadows.purpose: The index card resting on the board; also dropdowns and modals, which are cards pulled from the drawer.

shadows.name: lift-tray
shadows.purpose: Upward-cast only, so the tray reads as sliding out from under the card.

shadows.name: lift-key
shadows.purpose: The stamp key: inset top highlight plus short drop. A key you can press.

shadows.name: press-key
shadows.purpose: Active state of the stamp key; the stamp pressed into the stock.

shadows.name: board-recess
shadows.purpose: A dark wall at the drawer lip, falling away from the light. The only inset-on-surface effect in the system.

shadows.name: rail-seat
shadows.purpose: Hairline seat under the drawer-label rail where it meets the board.

shadows.name: focus-ring-field
shadows.purpose: Focused input field ring in stamp red.

motion.name: drawer-pull
motion.purpose: The single authored motion. Trays slide out from beneath a card that never moves.

motion.name: ease-drawer
motion.purpose: The only easing in the system.

motion.name: duration-reduced
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the drawer pull resolves instantly.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: The only shipped device class; there are no media-query breakpoints in the system.

texture.name: kraft-board

components.name: Status Plate

narrative.overview:
A label exists so you can find the thing again. The app is therefore the drawer you file it in, not a canvas you draw on. Kraft drawer board is the ground; the label under design is an index card lying on that board, and it is the brightest surface and the only true black ink on screen. Every other surface is furniture: raised kraft for keys, a typed plate for the drawer front, a card-stock tray that pulls out from under the card. Nothing floats over the artifact.

Density is low by intent and by device. This ships as a single Android phone app used one-handed, standing at the printer, so reach and target size outrank information density: tabs are 62x58, the commit key 109x58, every ghost and rail control at least 48px. The catalogue ships its measurements in a monospaced notation face with tabular figures, because a dimension that shifts width as it updates is a dimension you cannot read at a glance.

The world refuses the floating-toolbar mobile editor: no palette hovering over the work, no bottom sheet that shoves the card off screen. Tool surfaces slide out beneath a card that never moves. The shipped build also collapses Connect and Print into one state-dependent key in a single commit slot, so there is exactly one place a print begins, and the status rail carries state only.
keyCharacteristics: Kraft board ground, index-card stock for the artifact, stamp red for commit and nothing else
Square-cut stock: 2-4px radii, hairline rules, no soft pill geometry
The card never moves; trays pull out beneath it (measured displacement 0px)
Monospaced notation with tabular figures for every measurement, count and device id
One authored motion: the drawer pull. No fades, no springs, no ambient animation

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Stamp red marks commit and only commit. Delete, disconnect, and every destructive path use withdrawn grey with a strikethrough. If red appears on a control that does not print, it is a bug.

rules.name: The Brightest-Is-The-Artifact Rule
rules.body: The label card is the brightest surface and carries the only true black on screen. No chrome may out-brighten it; if a panel needs more light than the card, the panel is wrong.

rules.name: The Not-Alone Rule
rules.body: State is never carried by colour alone. The live dot changes shape as well as hue (6px circle when connected, 1px-radius square when faltering, hollow ring when empty), the disabled commit key switches to a dashed border, and every state carries a text label.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor
rules.body: Measured on the shipped build: filing line 6.15:1, tab label 6.15:1, status 7.2:1, commit key 9.54:1, wordmark on stock 12.72:1, disabled ghost 4.68:1. Nothing ships below 4.5:1.

rules.name: The Notation Rule
rules.body: Every measured quantity - millimetres, pixels, densities, counts, device ids, commit hashes - sets in the mono face with tabular figures. A number that changes width as it updates is unreadable at arm's length.

rules.name: The Named Key Rule
rules.body: Any control that commits or changes device state carries a word. Icon-only is permitted only for reversible, self-evident furniture (undo, redo, the overflow menu).

rules.name: The Bundled Face Rule
rules.body: No webfont is fetched at runtime. Both families are self-hosted variable woff2; the system stack is a fallback, never the shipped face.

rules.name: The Light-From-Above Rule
rules.body: Shadows fall downward from a fixed overhead source. The single exception is the tray, whose shadow casts upward precisely because it emerges from beneath the card.

rules.name: The No-Floating-Chrome Rule
rules.body: Nothing is elevated over the card. Panels, trays and menus occupy the board beside or beneath the artifact; the artifact is never eclipsed.

dos: Do keep stamp red for commit alone. One red control on screen at a time.
Do keep the card the brightest surface and the only true black on screen.
Do open tool surfaces from the bottom edge beneath a card that does not move. Measured displacement must stay 0px.
Do set every measurement in the notation face with tabular figures.
Do give every commit or device-state control a word alongside its glyph.
Do hold 48px as the touch floor and 58px for rail-level controls.
Do express disabled with a dedicated ink token and a shape change (dashed border), never with opacity alone.
Do carry state in shape and text as well as colour.
Do keep motion to the drawer pull (220ms cubicOut, 0ms reduced-motion) and honour prefers-reduced-motion.
Do cut stock square: 2-4px radii and 1px hairlines.
Do theme browser-native surfaces - selection, caret, scrollbars, focus ring - from the palette.
Do apply image-rendering: pixelated only at whole-number zoom, so the preview never misreports the print.
donts: Don't paint a destructive action red. Struck-through withdrawn grey is the destructive language.
Don't float a toolbar, palette, or sheet over the card. Chrome sits beside or beneath the artifact.
Don't add a second way to start a print or a connection. One commit slot, one state-dependent key.
Don't let a tray exceed 41% of the board height; a card you cannot see is a card you have left.
Don't introduce a fourth shadow token or a hard offset shadow. This world is lit from above and diffuse.
Don't fetch a font at runtime or fall back to a system display face.
Don't round past 4px or introduce pill and capsule geometry.
Don't add hover lifts, fades, springs, or ambient animation; the drawer pull is the whole motion vocabulary.
Don't scale the canvas backing store to fit the stage - scale CSS size only, so the drawn pixels stay the printed pixels.
Don't use a flat fill for the board; the kraft texture is the ground.
